title: Many hats, one message at a time
header_line: My analysis of one book on authority and personal brand. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Which hat are you wearing in this room?
A student said that my brand is many-sided: involved in multiple ventures, from schools to design, and leaning on my past as a builder and teacher. Another said I am also a father and family man.

I said that you can have multiple brands and multiple messages, and that I try to adapt and change hats depending on my audience. I said that I gave a talk to a group of children of very different ages and had to deliver the message in ten minutes.
I said that one of the things we can do is study the different identities we can develop.
A student said: in design there are a handful of people everyone looks up to. I follow how they gained authority. Once you build authority, you can monetize your time much better.
I said: you take your personality, perspective and message, and you scale it. That is what this book is about.
Which hat do you need to wear for your next audience?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the one message for each.
Write who you follow to learn how they gained authority.
Write how you could scale one message.

check.q: What did I say you can have?
What did I say I adapt to?
What did I say the book is about?

recap: Wear the right hat for the audience. Scale one message.
